title: Phoretic colloids (SIMD): the same Janus composites, formed from a random gas, travel 4.5-6.4 body lengths with their B cap held and then divide into two capped composites (3 such lineages on 3 seeds); the reciprocal twin neither travels nor divides. No wall, so not C:swim-divide
summary: World: 20261026T0356-c33-phoretic-divide-claim/world.py, unchanged (copied here). lineage.py now restarts a track's travel at every merge, so travel is measured on the same particles' body since its birth or last merge. Seed 0 (t=800): track 286, a composite of 103-128 particles with a B cap, travels 4.5 diameters along a smooth curve over t~424-537 and splits into 61 + 47, both with B (B share 0.23 each; swimdivide_seed0_track286.png); track 364 travels 5.3 diameters and splits 31 + 17 at generation 10. Seed 2 (t=400): track 177, a Janus composite of 32-41 particles, travels 6.4 diameters and splits into 16 + 13, both with B (swimdivide_seed2_track177.png). Seed 1: 0 of 55 persistent splits follow a >= 3 diameter merger-free travel (max 1.9). So swim-then-divide in one lineage happens 2, 0 and 1 times per seed, among 63, 55 and 14 persistent splits (swimdivide.txt). Matched reciprocal twin of the same turnover world (mu_A2 = +1, seed 0, t=400; reciprocal_turnover_seed0.png): 0 of 16 composites travel >= 3 diameters, 2 splits and 0 persistent, against 10 of 19 composites and 23 persistent splits without the change. Correction to the parent claim's limits: its count of dividing parents that had travelled >= 3 diameters (13/63, 17/55) included travel across merges; merge-free it is 2/63 and 0/55.

claims.statement: In runs from a uniform random particle mix, Janus composites (A body, B cap) grow on the closed food ledger, and some of them travel >= 3 body lengths with the cap held and then divide into two composites that each keep B: seed 0 tracks 286 (4.5 diameters, then 109 -> 61 + 47) and 364 (5.3, then 46 -> 31 + 17), seed 2 track 177 (6.4, then 33 -> 16 + 13); with reciprocal responses the same world gives neither travel nor division.
claims.track: seed 0, track 286 (swimdivide_seed0_track286.png): a capped composite travels 4.5 of its diameters merger-free from t~424 to t=537, keeps its B cap, and divides at t=537 into 61 + 47 particles, each with B share 0.23; the population it belongs to reaches generation 10 (research/alife/collective/contrib/20261026T0356-c33-phoretic-divide-claim/lineage_particles.txt)

controls_run.M: reciprocal_turnover_seed0.png and swimdivide.txt (mu_A2 = +1, same turnover world, seed 0, t=400): 0/16 composites travel >= 3 diameters vs 10/19
controls_run.D: same reciprocal twin: 0 persistent splits vs 23; the parent claim's turnover-off twin (tpack_off): 0-1 persistent splits

limits: Rare: 3 swim-then-divide lineages among 132 persistent splits on 3 seeds, none on seed 1; most divisions come from composites that grew by merging and moved little since. Seed 2's daughters are small (16 and 13 particles, just above the 12-particle body floor). Diameters are particle-cluster diameters (1.8 sqrt(n/pi)), not labkit body lengths; labkit packs of this world are the parent's (seeds 0, 1). The genealogy is reticulate (merges outnumber splits). There is no boundary layer (20261026T0441-c33-phoretic-no-wall), so this is SIMD, not SIBMD, and does not meet C:swim-divide. Food -> A/B conversion and decay are designed rules (E not claimed).
